We need to determine number of carbonyl groups in the sample's compound. We have no direct info about the compound. We can use IR spectra to detect C=O stretch, or carbon NMR to see carbonyl carbon shifts (~190-220 ppm). Use carbon_nmr_spectra tool (expensive) maybe cheaper to use IR first. IR will show carbonyl stretch around 1700 cm-1. That indicates presence of carbonyl groups. But need count. IR may show intensity but not count. Carbon NMR can show distinct carbonyl signals; each carbonyl carbon appears separate. Could also use HSQC but not needed.

We need to minimize cost. Perhaps use carbon_nmr_spectra to get carbon shifts and count signals in carbonyl region (190-220 ppm). That will give number of carbonyl carbons. Use carbon_nmr_spectra tool.

Let's call carbon_nmr_spectra.
